What each hair system is made of, and what that means for how it looks, breathes and lasts.
The base: lace, mono, skin and silk
The base decides everything: how natural it looks, how cool it feels, how long it lasts. The thinner the base, the better it looks and the sooner it wears.
Macro of a monofilament mesh base with hairs hand-tied into it as visible knots
Macro of a thin polyurethane base held between finger and thumb, hair passing through it
The finest, softest mesh. Its knots can be bleached until they vanish, which is why every hairline we fit is lace.
Monofilament: a fine, tough mesh. It breathes, takes the most hair, and outlasts every other base.
A clear polyurethane film, 0.08 to 0.10 mm thin. No mesh to see, so the hair seems to grow straight from the scalp.
Hair knotted onto a lace layer and drawn up through silk, so every knot sits hidden between the two. A parting shows scalp.
How the hair is tied in: knots and loops
Every hair is tied or looped into the base by hand. How it is tied decides how natural the root looks and how well it holds.
One small knot for each hair. Fine and flat, on lace and skin.
Each hair knotted twice, for the sides and back of a mono base.
Knots lightened until they disappear. Only lace takes it, so it is kept for the hairline.
No knot at all: each hair is looped through the skin, so it seems to grow from it.
Hair set into the skin so that it stands up from the root. Made for a parting or a brushed-back style.
The edges are where a hair system is held, and where it is seen.
A thin, transparent polyurethane edge. The tape grips it, never the mesh, and it disappears at the temples.
Polyurethane reinforced with mesh: stronger and slightly thicker, so it is kept to the sides and back, where nobody looks.
Up to an inch of lace along the hairline, its knots bleached until they disappear. It is what lets a hairline pass a close look, and every hair system we fit has one.

Density is how much hair is tied in, against a full natural head. More is not better: too much hair is what gives a hair system away. We match yours to the hair you still have at the sides, not the hair you had at twenty.
The scalp shows at a parting. For men over sixty.
Natural, without much volume. Most men's choice, and ours over forty.
Visibly fuller, and holds a style. For younger men, and men whose own hair is thick.

Will anyone be able to tell?

Not at conversational distance. The hairline is where it is won or lost, and every hair system we fit has a lace front that melts into the skin. Under a shower, or with a hand run back through the hair, someone could tell.
How long does a hair system last?

Months, not years: the base wears out before the hair does. How many depends on the base you choose, the heat and your care, and your technician tells you what to expect from yours. The monthly visit keeps it at its best.
What happens during the monthly service visit?
The technician lifts the hair system, cleans the adhesive off the base and your scalp, checks the knots, re-bonds it and trims the hair to match your own growth. About ninety minutes, at your home.
Can I swim, shower and exercise with it?
Yes to all three. Chlorine and sea salt shorten the life of the base, so rinse it in fresh water afterwards. Heavy sweating is fine.
Does it damage the hair I still have?
The base sits on skin, not on hair, and the perimeter is bonded to areas where you have little or none. Hair under the base is trimmed short rather than shaved.
How do you match the colour and the hairline?

Colour is matched against forty samples in daylight at the consultation, including the grey percentage. The hairline is drawn on your forehead with a pencil and agreed with you before anything is fitted.
What if I do not like it at the fit?
Say so before it's fitted and you pay nothing. Once it's fitted: if the fit isn't right, tell us within 14 days. We'll refit it free or refund you in full.
We come by pincode. Check yours on the booking page; if we're not there yet, leave your number and we'll tell you when we are.
It depends on the hair system you choose. Your technician quotes it at the free consultation, before anything is fitted. No deposit, no package.
Is this the same thing as a wig?
No. A wig sits on the whole head, is held by tension or clips, and comes off at night. This is bonded to the skin over the area you have lost, is cut to your face, and stays on for weeks at a time.

Straight answers on hair systems: how they compare with a transplant, and how they're fitted, cared for and priced.
Straight answers, before you book anything.
Hair system or transplant: what each involves, how soon you see a result, and who each suits.
Two answers to the same mirror. Here's how they differ.
A transplant moves hair you still have, usually from the back of your head, to where it has thinned. It is surgery, and the moved hair grows in over the months that follow.
A hair system is 100% real human hair on a fine base, shaped to your scalp and bonded over the area you've lost. Nothing is cut or moved, and you leave the visit with the look you chose.
A transplant takes months to show, and how full it ends up depends on how much hair you have to move.
A hair system shows the day it's fitted. Its density is matched to the hair at your sides, so it reads as yours, not as new.
A transplant asks for recovery time, and patience while the hair grows.
A hair system asks for a visit about once a month: your technician lifts it, cleans the base, bonds it again and keeps the cut sharp. The base wears in months, not years, and is renewed when it does.

If there's little hair left to move, or you'd rather avoid surgery, a hair system is the straighter road. If you have the hair to move and want something you never think about again, a transplant may suit you better: ask a surgeon.

At the same visit or a later one, as you prefer, the hair under the base is trimmed short, not shaved. The hair system is bonded to the skin, then cut into your own hair and styled. You see the result in the mirror before your technician leaves.
At home, at a time that suits you. All you need is a chair in good light and somewhere to wash hair.
Daily care for a hair system, what to do after a swim, and what happens at the monthly visit.
A few habits at home, and a visit about once a month.
Wash and style it like your own hair, gently. It doesn't grow, so the cut stays as it was left.
Heavy sweating is fine. After a swim in chlorine or the sea, rinse it in fresh water: both shorten the life of the base.

About once a month, your technician comes back to lift the hair system, clean the base and your scalp, bond it again and refresh the cut. It takes ninety minutes, and keeps it looking like the day it was fitted.
When it's time for a new one
The base wears before the hair does. When it does, your technician tells you, and your new hair system is matched to the last, so no one notices the change.
How long a hair system lasts
A hair system lasts months, not years. What decides how long yours lasts, and how to make it last longer.
Months, not years: the base wears before the hair does.

The base. A clear skin film looks the most natural and wears the soonest; monofilament mesh outlasts every other base. Heat, sea water and chlorine all shorten its life, and so does skipping the monthly visit.
Rinse it in fresh water after a swim, keep the monthly visit, and choose a base that suits how you live: a lace top for the gym and a Delhi summer, a skin base where nothing must show.
